title: IBU Podcast and Media Activities
text:
IBU Podcast is a media offering from International Burch University, produced and hosted by public relations professionals and students. It is based in the studio of the Department of Digital Communications and Public Relations, abbreviated as DCPR. The same studio hosts IBU Student Podcast, which features university students and provides a space for their ideas. The university page connects this student format with creativity and innovation.

The IBU Podcast page includes links to Spotify and Apple Podcasts, the university's YouTube channel and an RSS feed. A separate link leads to the student podcast. Visitors can suggest a topic for discussion with guests or submit a question through the university's contact page. The page therefore combines an introduction to the podcast, access to content on other platforms and an opportunity to suggest topics.

The published episode descriptions cover several subject areas. One conversation follows the transition from a basketball playing career to coaching, including team leadership and the development of young talent. The IBU Finals format expands the podcast project with a discussion of eSIM technology, modern communication, entrepreneurship and the challenges of the digital age. Its description includes increasingly demanding questions and a final challenge. Another episode considers mental preparation, stress, personal growth and burnout through professional sporting experience, with an emphasis on self-care. A conversation about dentistry covers digital platforms, continuous learning and the future of the profession.

Media activities also introduce students to radio practice. In a news item published on 22 October 2026, the university describes a visit to BH Radio 1 by first-year students from the Department of Digital Communications and Public Relations. The visit took place on 21 October as part of their Media Ecosystems course. At the headquarters of Radio and Television of Bosnia and Herzegovina, known as Sivi dom or the Grey Home, students learned about radio broadcasting and programme production.

Students explored the radio archives and listened to original archival recordings on equipment used during the Yugoslav era. This part of the visit addressed the importance of preserving audio heritage. They toured the radio drama recording studio, the main BH Radio 1 studio and the Federal Radio studio. According to the report, the experience connected classroom knowledge with practice and provided direct insight into radio's place within the media ecosystem.
